label: Web Search
title: Web Search
subtitle: Gives agents the ability to search the internet and read web pages. Useful for research, fact-checking, finding documentation, or gathering current information that is not in your knowledge base.
whenToUse: Use when an agent needs to find information that is not already in the project files or knowledge base — such as looking up a paper, checking current prices, reading documentation, or verifying a claim against a live source.

methods.name: Quick Search
methods.description: Returns titles, URLs, snippets, and the date the search provider has for each page, without visiting them. Fast and cheap; good for finding the right source before reading it. An agent can narrow a query to the last day, week, month, or year.

methods.name: Search Web
methods.description: Fetches and reads the top results for a query. Returns extracted text content with the date each page declares for itself, falling back to the search provider's date when the page declares none.

methods.name: Extract Web Page Content
methods.description: Reads a specific URL and returns its text, along with the date the page declares for itself — or a note that it declares none, so the agent can weigh how old a source is before quoting it. Use when you already know which page you want the agent to read. Web pages are read, and so are documents: a PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel or EPUB file at the URL is parsed into text rather than refused, and a CSV comes back a row at a time with its column names. A response above 5 MiB is refused, as is one that says it expands past 64 MiB, and a binary format with no text in it such as a bitmap image. The text it returns is capped at 10,000 characters by default and 100,000 at most, and a length that is not a positive whole number is refused. A reply that was cut says so, how long the text it read was — the whole page, or just the matched region when a filter was given — and whether raising the cap would return any more, so an agent can act on a partial page rather than work from one.

methods.name: Extract Links
methods.description: Returns all hyperlinks found on a page. Useful for discovering related resources or mapping a site structure. Accepts the same responses as Extract Web Page Content, so a binary or oversized page is refused rather than parsed.

methods.name: Search Web (JavaScript)
methods.description: Same as Search Web but uses a real browser to render JavaScript before extracting content. Needed for single-page apps and pages that load content dynamically. Reports the page's declared date the same way. The text it returns is capped at 10,000 characters, and the reply says when it was cut and how long the page really was, so an agent can narrow the URL rather than work from part of a page.

mediaCaption: A web search action card showing the query, sources visited, and extracted content returned to the agent
tips: Quick Search is significantly cheaper than full Search Web — use it first to find the best URL, then extract that specific page.
If an agent gets an empty or skeletal page, the content is probably drawn by JavaScript — try the rendering mode.
A page the agent cannot read says why: an unsupported type names the type it found, and an oversized one names the limit.
Not every result carries a date — a provider reports one only where it knows one, so an undated result is unknown-age rather than new.
